about: Every name clip made with Kokoro: what was said, by which voice, and when. Written by tools/voice/record_names.py. No clip has been checked by ear unless the catalogue says so.

kind_of_thing=plant:clue1.text: Think about things that grow in the ground.

kind_of_thing=plant:clue2.text: They are alive and they do not walk or fly.

kind_of_thing=plant:clue3.text: They have roots, stems, and leaves, and they make their own food.

kind_of_thing=plant:explanation.text: All of these are living things that grow in the ground. They have leaves and stems, and they stay in one place. Some grass is used to cover the ground in parks and lawns, and it is usually green.

part_we_eat=leaves:clue1.text: Think about the green, flat part of a plant that grows up in the sun.

part_we_eat=leaves:clue2.text: We pick this green part and cook it, but we do not dig it up from under the soil.

part_we_eat=leaves:clue3.text: We eat this soft green part, and we do not wait for a fruit or a seed to grow.

part_we_eat=leaves:explanation.text: We eat the green, leafy part of these plants. We pick the leaves and cook them, and we do not dig them up. Spinach leaves are full of iron, and they help keep your body strong.

where_it_travels=rails:clue1.text: Think about how a thing moves along a special path.

where_it_travels=rails:clue2.text: It rolls on two long metal lines.

where_it_travels=rails:clue3.text: It cannot turn away to the left or the right.

where_it_travels=rails:explanation.text: All of these move along metal lines on the ground. They cannot go anywhere else. A train can carry very heavy things, like coal, over long distances.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=wild_water:clue.text: Think about birds that spend lots of time in the water.
These birds find their food in the water.
These birds are not pets and do not live on a farm.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=wild_water:expl.text: These birds all live free and spend much of their time on or near water. They find their own food there. A penguin uses its flippers to swim under the water, but it cannot fly up in the air.

kind_of_thing=animal:clue1.text: Think about something that is alive and can move on its own.

kind_of_thing=animal:clue2.text: It can find its own food and eat it.

kind_of_thing=animal:clue3.text: It can have babies, and it breathes and grows.

kind_of_thing=animal:explanation.text: All of these are living things that move about and find their own food. They have bodies, and they breathe and eat. A hedgehog has thousands of sharp spines on its back, and it curls up when it feels scared.

kind_of_thing=nature_not_alive:clue1.text: Think about things you can see outside that are not alive.

kind_of_thing=nature_not_alive:clue2.text: These things are not animals and not plants.

kind_of_thing=nature_not_alive:clue3.text: People do not make these things; they are just there in the world.

kind_of_thing=nature_not_alive:explanati.text: These are all things we find in nature. They are not alive and nobody makes them. A mountain is a very big, high bump on the land.

kind_of_thing=made_by_people:clue1.text: Think about things that are not found growing or walking on their own.

kind_of_thing=made_by_people:clue2.text: People use their hands and tools to make these things.

kind_of_thing=made_by_people:clue3.text: These things would not be here if nobody had made them.

kind_of_thing=made_by_people:explanation.text: People make these things. They are not animals, plants, or things like the sun and rain. A bicycle has two wheels, and a person pushes the pedals with their feet to make it go.

kind_of_animal=mammal:clue1.text: Think about animals that drink their mother's milk when they are babies.

kind_of_animal=mammal:clue2.text: These animals have hair or fur on their bodies.

kind_of_animal=mammal:clue3.text: These animals are warm when you touch them, even when it is cold outside.

kind_of_animal=mammal:explanation.text: All these animals drink their mother's milk when they are small. They also have fur or hair on their bodies. A mother sheep is called a ewe, and her baby is called a lamb.

kind_of_animal=bird:clue1.text: Think about animals that have feathers.

kind_of_animal=bird:clue2.text: These animals have wings and a beak.

kind_of_animal=bird:clue3.text: Most of them can fly, but some cannot.

kind_of_animal=bird:explanation.text: All of these are birds. They have feathers, wings and a beak, and they lay eggs. A penguin uses its flippers to swim in the water, but it cannot fly in the air.

kind_of_animal=fish:clue1.text: Think about a creature that lives in water all its life.

kind_of_animal=fish:clue2.text: It breathes water through gills, not air.

kind_of_animal=fish:clue3.text: It has fins to swim and no legs at all.

kind_of_animal=fish:explanation.text: These animals all live in water and swim with fins. They breathe using gills. A goldfish can learn to push a small ball under the water.

kind_of_animal=reptile:clue1.text: Think of animals whose skin is dry and covered in scales.

kind_of_animal=reptile:clue2.text: These animals are cold when you touch them, and they lie in the sun to get warm.

kind_of_animal=reptile:clue3.text: These animals have scaly skin and most of them lay eggs on land, not in water.

kind_of_animal=dinosaur:clue1.text: Long, long ago, these animals lived on our Earth, and now we only see their bones.

kind_of_animal=dinosaur:clue2.text: Their bones are hard and old, and people dig them out of the ground to look at them.

kind_of_animal=dinosaur:clue3.text: These animals are not alive today at all — they all died out long before anyone's grandma was born.

kind_of_animal=dinosaur:explanation.text: These all lived very long ago and are gone now. We know them from the old bones people dig up. One of these had two rows of big flat plates on its back and long spikes on its tail.

kind_of_dinosaur=land_hunter:clue1.text: Think about a dinosaur that eats other animals.

kind_of_dinosaur=land_hunter:clue2.text: It hunts other dinosaurs on dry land, not in water or in the sky.

kind_of_dinosaur=land_hunter:clue3.text: It has strong legs for running after its food, and sharp teeth for eating it.

kind_of_dinosaur=flyer:clue1.text: Think about a creature up in the sky with big wings.

kind_of_dinosaur=flyer:clue2.text: This animal had wings and could fly, but it was not a bird.

kind_of_dinosaur=flyer:clue3.text: Its wings were made of skin, and it flew high above the ground.

kind_of_dinosaur=flyer:explanation.text: These are all flyers. They had wings and could fly in the sky. One of them was as tall as a giraffe when it stood on the ground.

kind_of_dinosaur=swimmer:clue1.text: Think about animals that live in the water all the time.

kind_of_dinosaur=swimmer:clue2.text: These animals swim in the sea and never walk on land.

kind_of_dinosaur=swimmer:clue3.text: They use flippers or paddles to move through the water.

kind_of_plant=flower:clue1.text: Think of a plant part that is pretty to look at and smells nice.

kind_of_plant=flower:clue2.text: This plant part is often put in a vase or given as a gift.

kind_of_plant=flower:clue3.text: Bees and butterflies come to this bright, colourful part of a plant.

kind_of_plant=flower:explanation.text: These are all plants with pretty, colourful parts that we love to look at and smell. A sunflower's big round head is really made of many tiny flowers packed together.

kind_of_plant=vegetable:clue1.text: Think about the plants we grow to eat at dinner.

kind_of_plant=vegetable:clue2.text: We cook and eat these plants, not just look at them.

kind_of_plant=vegetable:clue3.text: These plants go into our curry or our sabzi.

kind_of_plant=vegetable:explanation.text: We grow these plants to cook and eat them. They go into our food, not just into a vase or a garden. Garlic has a very strong smell and taste, so people use a little of it to make food taste better.

kind_of_nature=sky:clue1.text: Think about what you see when you look up high above your head.

kind_of_nature=sky:clue2.text: You can see these far away, but you cannot walk to them or touch them.

kind_of_nature=sky:clue3.text: They look like they float or shine up above, not down here on the ground.

kind_of_nature=water:clue1.text: Think about something wet you can see outside.

kind_of_nature=water:clue2.text: It is not alive, but plants and animals need it.

kind_of_nature=water:clue3.text: It can be big or small, and it stays in one place or moves.

kind_of_nature=water:explanation.text: These are all places where water sits or flows. You can see water in each one. A river starts small and gets bigger as it flows along.

kind_of_nature=land:clue1.text: Think about a place you can walk on, outside.

kind_of_nature=land:clue2.text: It is a part of the ground, not water or sky.

kind_of_nature=land:clue3.text: You can stand on it and look around.

kind_of_nature=land:explanation.text: These are all places on the land where you can go and stand. A hill is smaller than a mountain and not as steep.

kind_of_nature=ground:clue1.text: Think about the hard ground under your feet.

kind_of_nature=ground:clue2.text: You can pick it up, but it was never alive.

kind_of_nature=ground:clue3.text: It is not water, not sky, and not a place you live.

kind_of_nature=ground:explanation.text: These are all bits of the ground. They are not alive and you can touch them. Sand is made of tiny pieces of rock, smaller than gravel.

kind_of_made_thing=vehicle:clue1.text: Think about things that take people or loads from one place to another.

kind_of_made_thing=vehicle:clue2.text: You do not carry it in your hand; you sit in it or climb on it to go somewhere.

kind_of_made_thing=vehicle:clue3.text: It has wheels, or wings, or floats, and it moves you far away.

kind_of_made_thing=vehicle:explanation.text: These all carry people or things from one place to another. That is what we use them for. A helicopter can stop and stay still in the air above the ground.

kind_of_made_thing=toy:clue1.text: Think about things you play with.

kind_of_made_thing=toy:clue2.text: You hold them, move them, or make them go.

kind_of_made_thing=toy:clue3.text: They are made just for fun, not for work.

kind_of_made_thing=toy:explanation.text: These are all things made for children to play with and enjoy. A paper plane is a toy plane folded from paper that really glides through the air.

kind_of_made_thing=household:clue1.text: Think about the things you find inside a home.

kind_of_made_thing=household:clue2.text: You use these every day, and they stay in one place.

kind_of_made_thing=household:clue3.text: These are not for going places or for playing; they help you live at home.

kind_of_made_thing=household:explanation.text: These all belong inside a house, and we use them every day to live and keep things clean. A sponge is full of tiny holes, and when you rub it on something dirty, the dirt comes off.

kind_of_made_thing=tool:clue1.text: Think about something you hold in your hand to help you do a job.

kind_of_made_thing=tool:clue2.text: You use it to make or fix things, not to ride in or play with.

kind_of_made_thing=tool:clue3.text: It is hard and strong, and it helps your hand do work like hitting, digging or cutting.

kind_of_made_thing=tool:explanation.text: These all help our hands do hard work, like cutting, digging or fixing. A very old axe was probably the first tool people ever made, and it had no handle.

part_we_eat=fruit:clue1.text: Think about the part of the plant that holds the seeds inside.

part_we_eat=fruit:clue2.text: We eat this soft, round part that grows after the flower falls.

part_we_eat=fruit:clue3.text: You can see the little seeds inside when you cut it open.

part_we_eat=fruit:explanation.text: We eat these soft, ripe parts that grow from flowers. They hold the seeds inside them. A pumpkin is a fruit, and it can be orange, red, blue, or white.

part_we_eat=under_the_ground:clue1.text: Think about the part of a plant that hides down in the soil.

part_we_eat=under_the_ground:clue2.text: We dig it out of the ground to eat it.

part_we_eat=under_the_ground:clue3.text: It grows down low, under the dirt, not up high in the sun.

part_we_eat=under_the_ground:explanation.text: These plants all keep the part we eat down in the soil. We have to dig them out to eat them. The part of the potato we eat is a bumpy lump that grows under the ground.

part_we_eat=seeds_or_pods:clue1.text: Think about the little hard parts inside a plant that can grow into a new plant.

part_we_eat=seeds_or_pods:clue2.text: We take these out and cook them, not the soft juicy part around them.

part_we_eat=seeds_or_pods:clue3.text: We dry them and keep them in jars to eat later, like little hard bits.

part_we_eat=seeds_or_pods:explanation.text: We eat the small hard parts of these plants. They are the seeds we cook and eat. A pea you eat is really a tiny seed, and it is very light, less than a small coin's weight.

where_it_travels=road:clue1.text: Think about how people go from one place to another on land.

where_it_travels=road:clue2.text: These things roll on wheels and stop for people or goods.

where_it_travels=road:clue3.text: These things share the road with other traffic and need a driver or rider.

where_it_travels=road:explanation.text: These all carry people or goods along the road on wheels. A bicycle has two wheels, and a person pushes the pedals to make it go.

where_it_travels=water:clue1.text: Think about where a thing can move along, not on a hard path.

where_it_travels=water:clue2.text: It moves on something soft and wet that you can splash in.

where_it_travels=water:clue3.text: It floats and moves on the water, not on land or in the sky.

where_it_travels=water:explanation.text: All of these carry people or things while they float and move on water. A ship is big, and a boat is smaller, so a boat can be lifted up and carried on a ship.

where_it_travels=air:clue1.text: Think about something that goes high above your head.

where_it_travels=air:clue2.text: It does not need a road, a track, or water to move.

where_it_travels=air:clue3.text: It stays up in the sky while it carries people or things.

kind_of_house_thing=furniture:clue1.text: Think about the big, heavy things in a house that stay in one place.

kind_of_house_thing=furniture:clue2.text: You do not carry these around; they stay put and hold you or your things.

kind_of_house_thing=furniture:clue3.text: You sit on it, sleep on it, eat at it, or keep things inside it.

kind_of_house_thing=furniture:explanatio.text: These are all big things in a house that stay in one place. We sit on them, sleep on them, eat at them, or keep things inside them. A bed can come in different sizes, like single, double, and king size.

kind_of_house_thing=eating:clue1.text: Think about things we use when we are hungry or thirsty.

kind_of_house_thing=eating:clue2.text: We hold these in our hands at the table when we eat.

kind_of_house_thing=eating:clue3.text: We put food or drink on or in these, then it goes to our mouth.

kind_of_house_thing=eating:explanation.text: We use these at the table to eat and drink. They help the food and drink get to our mouth. A spoon is a tool we use to eat soft foods like soup and yogurt.

kind_of_house_thing=cleaning:clue1.text: Think about things that help make a place clean.

kind_of_house_thing=cleaning:clue2.text: You use them when something is dirty.

kind_of_house_thing=cleaning:clue3.text: They help you wash or sweep away the dirt.

kind_of_house_thing=cleaning:explanation.text: These all help us clean the house. We use them to wash, sweep and wipe things clean. A sponge is full of tiny holes, and when you rub it on something dirty, the dirt comes off.

kind_of_house_thing=electric:clue1.text: Think about things in your house that need power to work.

kind_of_house_thing=electric:clue2.text: These things stop working when the power goes off.

kind_of_house_thing=electric:clue3.text: You must plug these things in or switch them on to use them.

kind_of_house_thing=electric:explanation.text: These things all need electricity to work. When the power goes off, they stop. A light bulb makes light when electricity goes through it.

shape_of_the_land=high:clue1.text: Think about land that goes up, up, up.

shape_of_the_land=high:clue2.text: This land is tall and steep, not flat at all.

shape_of_the_land=high:clue3.text: You would have to climb up to stand on this land.

shape_of_the_land=high:explanation.text: All of these are tall, steep parts of the land that rise up high. A mountain is usually steeper and taller than a hill.

shape_of_the_land=hollow:clue1.text: Think about a place where the ground goes down, not up.

shape_of_the_land=hollow:clue2.text: It is a low or empty spot you could look down into.

shape_of_the_land=hollow:clue3.text: It is a dip or a hole in the ground, not a flat or high place.

shape_of_the_land=hollow:explanation.text: These are all places where the land goes down low. Some are big and some are small. A crater is a round dent on the ground, like a big bowl.

pet_farm_or_wild=pet:clue1.text: Think about an animal that lives inside your house with you.

pet_farm_or_wild=pet:clue2.text: This animal likes to stay close to people and be cared for by them.

pet_farm_or_wild=pet:clue3.text: People feed it, keep it safe, and it stays with the family at home.

pet_farm_or_wild=pet:explanation.text: These animals live with people in their homes. People feed them and take care of them every day. Dogs are popular pets because they are playful, friendly, and listen to people.

pet_farm_or_wild=farm:clue1.text: Think about animals that live where a farmer can look after them.

pet_farm_or_wild=farm:clue2.text: These animals give the farmer food or wool or eggs to use.

pet_farm_or_wild=farm:clue3.text: The farmer keeps them in a yard, a coop or a field, not in the house.

pet_farm_or_wild=farm:explanation.text: A farmer looks after these animals and keeps them for food, eggs or wool. A mother sheep is called a ewe, and her baby is called a lamb.

pet_farm_or_wild=wild_land:clue1.text: Think about animals that live far away from people.

pet_farm_or_wild=wild_land:clue2.text: They find their own food and make their own homes.

pet_farm_or_wild=wild_land:clue3.text: They live on the ground, not in water or in a house.

pet_farm_or_wild=wild_land:explanation.text: These animals all live free on land, away from homes and farms, and find their own food. A cheetah can run faster than any other animal on land, as fast as a car on a big road.

pet_farm_or_wild=wild_water:clue1.text: Think about a place that is full of water, like a big sea.

pet_farm_or_wild=wild_water:clue2.text: This animal spends most of its life in the water and comes up to breathe air.

pet_farm_or_wild=wild_water:clue3.text: This animal lives in the sea or a river, not in a house or a field.

pet_farm_or_wild=wild_water:explanation.text: They all live in the water and are wild animals. They swim in the sea, not in a house or on a farm. A whale breathes air from above the water, just like you and me.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=pet:clue1.text: Think of a bird that lives in a cage inside a house.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=pet:clue2.text: People feed this bird and keep it close to them every day.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=pet:clue3.text: This bird sits on a finger or in a cage at home, not in a field or a forest.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=pet:explanation.text: These birds live with people in their homes. People feed them and keep them close. Some of these birds can copy the sounds people make, like talking.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=farm:clue1.text: Think about birds that live with people who grow food.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=farm:clue2.text: People keep these birds in a yard or a little house.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=farm:clue3.text: People raise these birds to eat them or to sell their eggs and meat.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=farm:explanatio.text: People raise these birds on a farm. They keep them for eggs and meat. People in America eat turkey on a special day called Thanksgiving.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=wild_land:clue1.text: Think about a bird that lives free, not in a house or a cage.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=wild_land:clue2.text: It flies in the open sky and finds its own food.

pet_farm_or_wild_of_bird=wild_land:clue3.text: It does not live with people or on a farm.

what_people_do_there=pray:clue1.text: Think of a place where people go to talk to God.

what_people_do_there=pray:clue2.text: People go there to sing, to pray, and to be quiet with God.

what_people_do_there=pray:clue3.text: People sit together there and fold their hands to pray.

what_people_do_there=pray:explanation.text: People go to these buildings to pray and to be close to God. In a gurdwara, everyone can sit and eat a free meal together.

what_people_do_there=buy:clue1.text: Think about a place where money and things change hands.

what_people_do_there=buy:clue2.text: People come here to get things they need or want, and they pay for them.

what_people_do_there=buy:clue3.text: Here you can pick a thing up, pay money for it, and carry it home.

what_people_do_there=buy:explanation.text: In all these places, people give money and take home things they need or want. A market is a place where people go to buy or sell things.

what_people_do_there=travel:clue1.text: Think about a place where you go to begin a trip far away.

what_people_do_there=travel:clue2.text: People wait there with bags, ready to go somewhere new.

what_people_do_there=travel:clue3.text: You go there to get on a big thing that carries you away.

what_people_do_there=travel:explanation.text: People come to these places to start a trip. They get on a train, plane, or boat and go. The busiest railway station in the world is in Tokyo, Japan.

what_people_do_there=cross:clue1.text: Think about going from one side to the other side.

what_people_do_there=cross:clue2.text: You do not stay here; you go across or go up.

what_people_do_there=cross:clue3.text: It helps you get over something, like water or a road.

what_people_do_there=cross:explanation.text: These are all places where you cross over something or climb up high. You use them to get to the other side or to go up. People have walked across bridges for thousands of years.

how_we_play_with_it=build:clue1.text: Think about making something new with your hands.

how_we_play_with_it=build:clue2.text: You put the pieces one on top of another.

how_we_play_with_it=build:clue3.text: When you finish, you have made a shape or a thing.

how_we_play_with_it=build:explanation.text: These toys are for making things. You put the pieces together to build something. You can press the blocks together and they stick, so you can build big things.

how_we_play_with_it=pretend:clue1.text: Think about a toy you hold close and love.

how_we_play_with_it=pretend:clue2.text: This toy is soft or small, and you use it in your arms or in make-believe.

how_we_play_with_it=pretend:clue3.text: You hug it, or you act like it is real in a story.

how_we_play_with_it=pretend:explanation.text: These toys are for hugging and for pretend play. You hold them close or make up stories with them. A teddy bear is a soft toy that looks like a baby bear.

how_we_play_with_it=fly:clue1.text: Think about a toy that goes up in the air and floats.

how_we_play_with_it=fly:clue2.text: You hold it with a string or your hand, and the air lifts it.

how_we_play_with_it=fly:clue3.text: It moves through the air above you, not on the ground.

how_we_play_with_it=fly:explanation.text: These toys all go up and float in the moving air. You let the wind carry them. In India, people fly kites on Makar Sankranti.

how_we_play_with_it=music:clue1.text: Think about toys that make sounds you can hear.

how_we_play_with_it=music:clue2.text: You use your hands or your mouth to make the sound come out.

how_we_play_with_it=music:clue3.text: The sound is music, not a bang or a beep.

kind_of_animal=reptile:explanation.text: They all have dry, scaly skin and lay their eggs on land. That is what makes them one family. A turtle has a hard shell that keeps it safe from other animals.

kind_of_plant=grass_grain:clue1.text: Think about plants with long, thin leaves.

kind_of_plant=grass_grain:clue2.text: These plants grow in big open fields, not in pots.

kind_of_plant=grass_grain:clue3.text: Many of these plants give us food we eat every day.

kind_of_nature=sky:explanation.text: These are all things you can see up high in the sky, far above the ground. The Sun is really a star, and it is the star closest to us.

kind_of_made_thing=building:clue1.text: Think about places you can go inside or walk on.

kind_of_made_thing=building:clue2.text: People go to these places to do something or to get something.

kind_of_made_thing=building:clue3.text: Some are big and some are small, but people made them all.

kind_of_made_thing=building:explanation.text: People made all of these. We go to them for many things, like praying, learning, shopping or crossing a road. A footbridge is a bridge made just for people to walk on, not for cars.

where_it_travels=air:explanation.text: These all travel high up in the sky, not on the ground or on water. A helicopter can stop and stay in one place above the ground.

kind_of_dinosaur=land_grazer:clue1.text: Think about a dinosaur that eats green plants all day.

kind_of_dinosaur=land_grazer:clue2.text: This dinosaur walks on the ground and eats plants, not meat.

kind_of_dinosaur=land_grazer:clue3.text: This plant-eater stays on land and never flies or swims.

kind_of_dinosaur=land_grazer:explanation.text: All of these dinosaurs stayed on land and ate plants. They did not hunt other animals, fly, or swim. One of these plant-eaters had a long neck to reach leaves high in the trees.

kind_of_dinosaur=swimmer:explanation.text: These animals all lived in the water and swam to move around. One of these sea animals had a smaller sea animal inside its tummy!

dinosaur_group=long_necked:clue1.text: Think about a very long neck reaching up high.

dinosaur_group=long_necked:clue2.text: These dinosaurs had long necks and ate plants all day.

dinosaur_group=long_necked:clue3.text: They walked on four legs and stretched their necks to eat leaves.

dinosaur_group=long_necked:explanation.text: These dinosaurs all had very long necks and ate plants. They used their long necks to reach leaves high up. One of these dinosaurs, Brachiosaurus, could reach leaves as high as a tall building.

dinosaur_group=horned:clue1.text: Think about a head with something special on top.

dinosaur_group=horned:clue2.text: Some of these heads have pointy parts sticking out.

dinosaur_group=horned:clue3.text: Their heads also have a big bony shield behind the pointy parts.

dinosaur_group=horned:explanation.text: These dinosaurs all have horns and a big bony shield on their heads. That is why they go together in one group. Triceratops had three horns on its head, and its name even means three horned face.

kind_of_plant=grass_grain:explanation.text: These plants all have long, thin leaves and grow close together in fields. We eat them or use them to make food. Bamboo is a giant grass, and it can grow very tall, as tall as a big tree.

kind_of_dinosaur=land_hunter:explanation.text: These dinosaurs all hunted other animals for food, and they walked and ran on land. The T. rex had a bite so strong it could break the bones of smaller dinosaurs.

what_it_eats=eats_plants:clue1.text: Think about what grows green in the ground.

what_it_eats=eats_plants:clue2.text: This animal's tummy is happy with grass and leaves.

what_it_eats=eats_plants:clue3.text: It never wants meat or bugs, only green things.

what_it_eats=eats_plants:explanation.text: These animals all fill their tummies with grass and leaves. They never eat meat or bugs. A giraffe is the tallest animal that lives on land.

what_it_eats=eats_meat:explanation.text: These animals all hunt other animals and eat their meat. That is why they belong together. A cheetah can run very fast, as fast as 105 kilometres in one hour.

what_it_eats=eats_insects:clue1.text: Think about tiny crawling things with six legs.

what_it_eats=eats_insects:clue2.text: These animals hunt for very small bugs to fill their tummies.

what_it_eats=eats_insects:clue3.text: They use long noses or sticky tongues to catch little bugs.

what_it_eats=eats_insects:explanation.text: These animals all eat mostly tiny bugs like ants and insects. That is their main food. An anteater's tongue can be as long as a grown-up's arm, and it is sticky to catch ants.

what_it_eats=eats_meat:clue1.text: This animal eats other animals, not plants.

what_it_eats=eats_meat:clue2.text: It hunts other animals and eats only their meat.

what_it_eats=eats_meat:clue3.text: Its food is meat, and it never eats plants or bugs.

what_it_eats=eats_both:clue1.text: This animal eats two kinds of food, not just one.

what_it_eats=eats_both:clue2.text: It eats green things that grow, and also eats other animals.

what_it_eats=eats_both:clue3.text: Its tummy gets full from plants and from meat too.

what_it_eats=eats_both:explanation.text: These animals eat both plants and meat, so they belong together. A raccoon eats many things, like fruit, nuts, insects, and even frogs.

kind_of_plant=tree:explanation.text: These all grow tall with a hard trunk and branches up high. They are big plants that live for many years. The coconut tree can grow as tall as 30 metres, which is taller than many houses.

kind_of_animal=insect:clue1.text: Think about tiny creatures with six legs.

kind_of_animal=insect:clue2.text: These little creatures often have wings too.

kind_of_animal=insect:clue3.text: You can see many of them buzzing or crawling near you.

kind_of_plant=tree:clue1.text: Think about a plant with a big, hard stem called a trunk.

kind_of_plant=tree:clue2.text: This plant grows very tall and has branches up high.

kind_of_plant=tree:clue3.text: Birds like to sit and rest in this tall plant.

kind_of_animal=insect:explanation.text: These little creatures all have six legs and a hard shell outside. Many of them can fly or buzz around us. A ladybug has bright red wings with black spots to warn other animals to stay away.

how_it_makes_sound=hit_or_strike:clue1.text: Think about how your hand makes a sound on something.

how_it_makes_sound=hit_or_strike:clue2.text: You use a stick or your hand to tap it.

how_it_makes_sound=hit_or_strike:clue3.text: When you tap or bang it, it makes a loud sound.

how_it_makes_sound=hit_or_strike:explana.text: You make these sounds by hitting them. Your hand or a stick taps them, and they ring or rattle. A tambourine is like a little drum you hold in your hand, and it has tiny jingles around the edge.

how_it_makes_sound=blow_into:clue1.text: You use your breath to make the sound.

how_it_makes_sound=blow_into:clue2.text: Your mouth goes on it, and the air goes in.

how_it_makes_sound=blow_into:clue3.text: You blow in, and the air makes the music.

how_it_makes_sound=blow_into:explanation.text: You make music with these by blowing your breath into them. A harmonica is small, and you play it by blowing into holes in its side.

how_it_makes_sound=pluck_strings:clue1.text: Think about how your fingers touch the toy to start the sound.

how_it_makes_sound=pluck_strings:clue2.text: You move your fingers along tight lines to make the sound.

how_it_makes_sound=pluck_strings:clue3.text: Your fingers pull or sweep the tight lines, and they are not keys or holes.

how_it_makes_sound=press_keys:clue1.text: Think about a toy you play with your fingers.

how_it_makes_sound=press_keys:clue2.text: You do not hit it or blow it or pull its strings.

how_it_makes_sound=press_keys:clue3.text: You touch small parts on top, and music comes out.

how_it_makes_sound=pluck_strings:explana.text: You make music on all of these by pulling or sweeping your fingers over tight strings. A small one of these has just four strings to pull and play.

how_it_makes_sound=press_keys:explanatio.text: You play all of these with your fingers on little parts. When you touch them, music comes out. A toy piano makes its sound from little round metal rods inside, not from strings.

how_we_play_with_it=music:explanation.text: All of these make music when you play them. You can shake, blow or tap them to hear a sound. A recorder is a tube you blow into, and it sounds a bit like a bird singing.
